root_cause.text: The ath12k WoW code incorrectly applied wake/offload configuration to every MLO link vdev in `ar->arvifs` instead of restricting it to the primary/default link (`ahvif->deflink`), causing unsupported duplicate WoW offloads on secondary links and firmware crashes on WCN7850.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (arvif != &arvif->ahvif->deflink) continue;` in all WoW-related per-vif loops (`ath12k_wow_cleanup`, `ath12k_wow_set_wakeups`, `ath12k_wow_nlo_cleanup`, `ath12k_wow_arp_ns_offload`, `ath12k_gtk_rekey_offload`), and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that in multi-link connections the firmware crashes because “WoW offloads [were] enabled on both primary and secondary links.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict WoW vif cleanup to default-link interfaces so non-default links are skipped during cleanup.
intent_record.what: A conditional check was added inside the loop over `ar->arvifs` to skip entries where `arvif` is not equal to `&arvif->ahvif->deflink`, using `continue` before calling `ath12k_wow_vif_cleanup(arvif)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the cleanup now runs only for the default link interface of each ahvif and avoids invoking WoW vif cleanup on non-default link entries, preventing duplicate or inappropriate cleanup on additional links.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip non-default link interfaces when configuring WoW wakeups so wakeup settings are applied only to the default vdev.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added inside the arvif iteration to skip entries where `arvif` is not equal to `&arvif->ahvif->deflink`, followed by `continue;`, before the existing P2P vdev skip logic and wakeup configuration call.
intent_record.how: At runtime, wakeup configuration is now applied only to the default link interface for each ahvif and not to non-default link entries encountered in the list. This prevents `ath12k_wow_vif_set_wakeups()` from being invoked on secondary or non-default links, avoiding incorrect WoW wakeup setup on those vdevs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict WoW NLO cleanup to default-link interfaces so non-default links are skipped and not cleaned up incorrectly.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added at the start of the list iteration in ath12k_wow_nlo_cleanup(): if the current arvif is not equal to arvif->ahvif->deflink, the loop skips that entry with continue.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the cleanup now only processes the default link for each ahvif and ignores non-default link entries, preventing wow NLO cleanup logic from running on secondary or non-default links during iteration.

intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added inside the arvif iteration loop to compare the current arvif against ahvif->deflink, and to skip the iteration with continue when they do not match.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the ARP/NS offload logic now runs only for the default link interface and ignores non-default link arvif entries, preventing the function from applying STA-specific WoW offload handling to additional link contexts.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict GTK rekey offload handling to the default link vif to avoid processing non-default link entries.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause by limiting WoW cleanup, wakeup, and offload handling to the default/primary link vif and skipping non-default MLO links, preventing duplicate unsupported WoW offloads on secondary links.

candidates.rationale: This loop iterates over every vdev in ar->arvifs, which is the core bug: WoW wakeup configuration was applied to all MLO link vdevs instead of being restricted to the primary/default link.
This directly applies WoW wakeup settings to each iterated arvif, causing unsupported duplicate wake/offload programming on secondary links.
For ARP/NS offload handling, iterating over all arvifs includes non-default MLO links, matching the root cause of offload configuration being incorrectly applied beyond the default link.
GTK rekey offload logic also walks all link vdevs instead of only the default link, enabling duplicate offloads on unsupported secondary links.
Cleanup is invoked for every arvif from the full ar->arvifs iteration, reflecting the same faulty assumption that all link vdevs should participate in WoW handling.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the relevant WoW configuration logic and is sufficient to determine the issue. The root cause is applying WoW setup/cleanup to every MLO link vdev in `ar->arvifs` instead of restricting it to the primary/default link. That exact construct is present here: `ath12k_wow_cleanup()` does `list_for_each_entry(arvif, &ar->arvifs, list) { ret = ath12k_wow_vif_cleanup(arvif); ... }`, and `ath12k_wow_set_wakeups()` likewise does `list_for_each_entry(arvif, &ar->arvifs, list) { ret = ath12k_vif_wow_set_wakeups(arvif, wowlan); ... }`. There is no check to limit operations to `ahvif->deflink` or otherwise skip secondary MLO links. Instead, `ath12k_vif_wow_set_wakeups()` unconditionally programs patterns and wake events for the passed `arvif` via calls such as `ath12k_wmi_wow_add_pattern(ar, arvif->vdev_id, ...)` and `ath12k_wmi_wow_add_wakeup_event(ar, arvif->vdev_id, i, 1)`. Similarly cleanup removes events/patterns for every vdev. Because the code iterates over all `ar->arvifs` and lacks any default-link restriction, the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not yet present.

The vulnerable construct is present in `ath12k_wow_set_wakeups()`: `list_for_each_entry(arvif, &ar->arvifs, list) { ... ret = ath12k_wow_vif_set_wakeups(arvif, wowlan); ... }`. This iterates over every vdev in `ar->arvifs` and applies WoW wakeups, including `wowlan->nd_config` handling inside `ath12k_wow_vif_set_wakeups()`.
